findings.title: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by Recover
findings.description: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

adjudication.why: The login bean previously called findFirst().get() without a guard. This patch replaces the lookup with one that also checks federated credentials. The raw-list type-safety concern is compiler/linter territory and does not establish the claimed new absent-credential failure.

findings.title: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.r
findings.description: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication.why: The new user-storage getCredentials path creates a recovery model with createFromValues but never transfers the stored ID. createFromValues does not set an ID, while the authenticator later passes getId to removal.
